60-unsatisfactory-standing-faculty-of-en: CGPA below 1.20, or TGPA under 2.50 with CGPA under 2.00.
Fall (Interim): continue at 13 credits at most, and end the term with CGPA 2.00+ or TGPA 2.50+. See an adviser before withdrawal deadlines.

Winter: you must leave the Faculty for at least one term. If you're readmitted and fall Unsatisfactory again, you can't continue, and must leave for a term or permanently according to your last readmission letter.
60-academic-standing-faculty-of-law: A sessional GPA (Fall and Winter together) under 1.50 means withdrawing, unless the Admissions Committee allows otherwise for exceptional reasons.
From 1.50 to 1.99 you continue, but need a later sessional GPA of 2.50 or CGPA of 2.00. Graduating takes a 2.00 CGPA.
60-academic-standing-school-of-continuin: In Unsatisfactory Standing, apply to your academic area's Appeals Committee.
60-myprogress: A degree audit tool that compares your record to your curriculum, shows what's left, and records approved exceptions such as a substituted course.
It's only an advising aid, and doesn't approve you to graduate. Open to selected faculties.
60-student-record-changes: Covers adding, dropping or withdrawing from courses, withdrawing from McGill, changing programs, status changes such as leave, exchange or term away, and tuition status changes through legal documents.
60-before-registrar-deadlines: After normal deadlines but before Registrar Deadlines, write to your Associate Dean or Director explaining why you couldn't ask sooner.
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, 3415 McTavish, with an OASIS or SOUSA adviser.
61-after-registrar-deadlines: Normally refused. Only unforeseeable, extraordinary personal or academic circumstances are considered, on request to your Associate Dean or Director. A fee may apply, and the faculty must document it for Enrolment Services (except grade changes).
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, with an adviser.
61-fee-assessment-consequences: The new charge shows on your next statement. To contest it, write to Enrolment Services, who review your faculty's documents with Student Accounts if needed and reply to you.
61-student-s-citizenship-immigration-or-: Faculties don't handle these; see the legal documents section (p. 28). A fee may apply after the deadline.
62-examinations-general-information: Exams follow the Exam Regulations and the Policy on Assessment of Student Learning, both on the Secretariat site. Check the Exams website and your faculty's own rules too.
62-credit-by-examination: Exceptionally, some faculties let you ask your Associate Dean or Director to take a final for credit without registering, only in courses assessed by the final alone.
63-undergraduate-advising: There are faculty and degree advisers, departmental advisers, professors and peers. The types below show who to see.
63-advising-and-the-university-mission: Advising is part of McGill's educational mission and happens in many places. Your Faculty's site and the Academic Advising site explain where.
63-the-role-of-student-advising: Seek advice actively. Advisers guide you, but meeting requirements and knowing the rules is ultimately on you.
63-faculty-specific-regulations: McGill has 12 Faculties, and you belong to one. Your offer letter gives your Faculty, degree, program and credits to complete.
63-your-academic-program: You're in a degree, usually with programs such as majors and minors. B.Eng. students normally follow one, and B.A. students more than one.

A typical degree is 120–140 credits over four years. CEGEP students usually get 30 credits of Advanced Standing, leaving 90–110 from U1. Others usually start in U0, the Foundation year. IB, French Baccalaureate, AP and transfers vary.
Requirements are in your faculty or department's section, even for a program in another faculty, such as a B.Com. with a minor in Arts.
Three credits is typically a one-term course. Departments may offer recommended streams or handbooks.
Conversations with advisers are confidential, and some matters need more than one to sign off.
Faculty advisers, in Student Affairs all year, know the degree rules, help with program choice, load and deadlines, exchanges and awards, and support you through difficulties.

Departmental advisers, available at set times, guide course selection for a major or minor, assess equivalencies and transfer credit, and usually confirm you've met requirements. Check in before your final year.
Professors can mentor you on trends, readings and research, and send you to advisers for signatures. Peer advisers are trained students with drop-in hours, in some units.
64-related-resources: Campus Life and Engagement helps new students find their way. The Student Wellness Hub has counsellors, social workers and psychologists, with drop-ins and crisis help, and Local Wellness Advisors work across faculties.
CaPS helps with careers and jobs. Service Point, 3415 McTavish, handles official documents, records, fees and exchanges. At Macdonald, it's Laird Hall, Room 106.
The WELL Office serves Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and Communication Sciences students. Medical Learner Affairs serves UGME and PGME students.
65-internships-and-co-op-programs: Agriculture: Experiential Learning and Community Outreach. Arts: Arts Internships. Education: B.Ed. field experience through Internships and Student Affairs; Kinesiology through your KPE adviser.
Engineering: Internship Program (p. 745), plus co-ops in Mining and Materials. Law: International Human Rights Internships. Management: BCom Internships.
Science, plus Arts and B.A. & Sc. students majoring in Computer Science, Geography, Mathematics, Psychology, Environment or Software Engineering: Science Internship Program.
65-exchange-programs: McGill Abroad covers exchanges, funding and pre-departure help.
Details: Arts OASIS; Engineering Student Affairs; Law's Exchange and Study-Away page; Management (p. 911); SOUSA for Science and B.A. & Sc.; Music's Learning Abroad page and Student Affairs.
65-field-study-semesters: See the Field Study Semesters page.
65-mobility-bursary-for-exchanges: Helps pay for studying abroad within your degree. See McGill Abroad's Funding page.
66-overview: You must finish faculty and program requirements, be in Satisfactory Standing and have a CGPA of at least 2.00; some faculties ask more. See your adviser early in your last year.
After Senate approval, transcripts show "Degree Granted" and your record is final, with no more changes.

Fall: courses by end of December, apply by end of November, degree in February, Spring convocation. Winter: end of April, apply by end of February, degree in May, Spring convocation. Summer: end of August, apply by mid-May, degree in October, Fall convocation.
66-minimum-residency-requirement: At least 60 McGill credits for an undergraduate degree, or for a second one. Some programs add limits, such as two-thirds of program requirements done at McGill. Check your faculty's section. Graduate programs have their own.
66-apply-to-graduate: Most undergraduates and non-thesis graduate students apply in Minerva (Student Records, Apply for Graduation) once registered for their final year. You must tell McGill you intend to graduate. Medicine and Dentistry students are flagged automatically.
Applying confirms that your curriculum is right and that you'll have finished by that term.

Unless you submit an Opposition Form by April 15 (Spring) or September 15 (Fall), your details are shared for the program and broadcast, regalia, photographer, your professional order, and a digital diploma through ARUCC's MyCreds™ / MesCertif™, whose terms apply if you use it. Opting out doesn't affect your degree.
67-deadlines: Same dates as above. If you miss one, contact Student Affairs at once. Arts and Science students file a Graduation Term Change Request and see an adviser.
Continuing Studies certificates and diplomas don't need 60 credits. Graduate students follow the GPS Graduating page. Physical and Occupational Therapy students need a 2.30 CGPA.
67-graduation-approval: Follow it in Minerva's Graduation Approval Query from early January (Fall), early April (Winter) or early September (Summer).
"Faculty Approved" comes first; "Degree Granted" follows Senate approval in late February, late May or late October.
67-graduation-honours-dean-s-honour-list: 60+ McGill credits and in the top 10% of your faculty's graduating class by CGPA. Transfer students may lose it if their earlier CGPA isn't comparable.
67-distinction: 60+ McGill credits and in the top 25% but not the top 10%, by CGPA. Same transfer condition. Not given by Education, Dentistry, Law, Medicine or Continuing Studies.
67-faculty-of-science-dean-s-multidiscip: Recognizes B.Sc. and B.A. & Sc. students with broad research: 9+ credits of approved research courses for a letter grade, one of 3+ credits from another unit, all C or above, averaging 3.0 or above. It's noted on your transcript.
S grades in Winter 2020 to Winter 2021 count exceptionally toward the 9 credits, though not the average.
68-application: Automatic if your courses are on the approved list. To count another research course, one with a project and substantive report, ask SOUSA at least four months before graduating (February 1 for June, July 1 for November, August 1 for February). Reading courses, BASC 396 and 449, and Arts courses don't qualify.
68-honours-and-first-class-honours-for-f: Your department recommends you if you meet its requirements: CGPA 3.00 for Honours, 3.50 for First-Class. Joint Honours students must qualify in both parts, and some departments ask more.
Below 3.00, see your adviser about graduating in another program.
Same thresholds: 3.00 and 3.50 at graduation, all program requirements done, possibly more by program. Below that, ask your adviser about another program.
68-outstanding-achievement-for-schulich-: Departments may recommend this for superior performance on an instrument or voice, or in an academic discipline.
68-required-documents: Diplomas are given at convocation in May/June or October/November, and not before, as the parchment bears that date.
68-replacing-a-lost-diploma: Order and pay, including courier, in the ES Services eStore.
68-requesting-a-diploma-following-your-c: Didn't attend? Order courier delivery on the eStore or book a pick-up with Service Point. Unclaimed diplomas are kept two years and then destroyed, after which you'd pay for a replacement.
68-modifying-the-name-on-your-diploma: First change your name with a Personal Data Change Form and documents (p. 30). Once it's confirmed, order and pay for a replacement on the eStore.
69-certified-copies: Enrolment Services certifies copies and issues translations: into English from Latin, or into French from English or Latin.
From Spring 2026, parchments are in English for all degrees but the Executive MBA. Before that, English or Latin depending on the degree.
69-submitting-your-request: All diploma requests go through the ES Services eStore.
69-aegrotat-standing-and-degree: A rare degree for students in Satisfactory Standing who've done 75%+ of requirements but can't finish because of a serious medical or similar situation.
Your Dean asks the Associate Provost (Student Life and Learning). It shows in the convocation program, not on the transcript.
70-admission-to-professional-and-graduat: Heading for Dentistry, Law or Medicine? Ask those faculties about prerequisites.
70-language-requirements-for-professions: Québec law requires French to enter a professional order. Show it by three years full-time in French post-primary school, by passing French mother tongue exams in Secondary 4 or 5, by finishing secondary school in Québec in 1986 or later, or by passing the OQLF exam.

Registered students within two years of such a degree can write the OQLF exam, held every three months with no limit on attempts, and priority to those closest to graduating. Enrolment Services has the form. OQLF: 125 Sherbrooke St. W.

Learn French at the French Language Centre or Continuing Studies (688 Sherbrooke St. W.), or keep it up in French Language and Literature. Some Continuing Studies language courses don't count toward your degree.

McGill degrees give access to orders for agrologists, architects, accountants (chartered, industrial administration, licensed general), chartered appraisers, chemists, dentists, dietitians, engineers, geologists, industrial relations counsellors, lawyers, nurse clinicians, occupational therapists, physicians, physiotherapists, psychologists, social workers, speech therapists and audiologists, urbanists, and vocational guidance counsellors.
70-graduate-programs: Over 250 doctoral and master's programs in more than 85 fields. See mcgill.ca/gradapplicants and the catalogue's graduate section.
71-university-government: McGill is a corporation under a Royal Charter, with the Crown's supervisory power exercised by the Governor General as Visitor.

The Board of Governors, the Royal Institution for the Advancement of Learning under Québec law, manages finances and appoints professors. Members: 12 elected by the Board, 3 by alumni, 2 by Senate, 2 by administrative and support staff, 2 by academic staff, 2 by students, plus the Chancellor and President ex officio.
The Chancellor presides over Convocation and joint meetings. The President and Vice-Chancellor is chief executive and chairs Senate.
Senate is the top academic authority, over admission, courses, discipline and degrees, and faculties carry out its rules.
71-the-visitor: Mary Simon, Governor General and Commander-in-Chief of Canada, as Administrator of the Government of Canada. The Board has 25 voting members as of July 1, 2024.
71-members-at-large: Arun Bajaj, Maryse Bertrand (Chair), Bertrand Cesvet, Gregory David, Ariel Deckelbaum, Alan Desnoyers, Fred Headon, Pierre Matuszewski (Vice-Chair), Maarika Paul (Vice-Chair), Diletta Prando, Samira Sakhia, Jonathan Sigler.
71-student-representatives: One from SSMU and one from PGSS.
71-two-non-voting-student-observers-voic: One from MACES and one from MCSS. Profiles are on the Board's membership page.
72-senate-ex-officio: Chancellor, Board Chair, President, Provost, Deputy Provost and vice-presidents, deans of faculties, Continuing Studies, Graduate Studies, Students and Libraries, the Registrar, and the Director of Teaching and Learning Services.
72-elected-members: 65 elected by faculties, libraries, the Board, and administrative and support staff; 21 students.
72-administration: Senior administration, the Board and Senate provide direction and oversight through formal decision-making. See About McGill's Administration and Governance.

73-student-governance: SSMU represents all 22,000+ downtown undergraduates, with six elected executives and a Legislative Council of 37 that meets every two weeks. It runs over 250 clubs and 19 services, plus events like Orientation Week, Activities Night and Faculty Olympics.
It has a five-floor building with lounge, cafeteria, bar and spaces for groups. Offices: 3600 McTavish, Suite 1200, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

MACES represents those whose records are run by Continuing Studies. Founded 1985, incorporated 1989, accredited 1990. It has a free computer lab, Microsoft courses and study and social spaces at 3437 Peel, with an elected board. Students in several programs may belong to several associations.
74-facilities-and-residences: Treat facilities with respect. Facilities Management and Ancillary Services has details.
74-residential-facilities: Various housing types on both campuses.
74-mission-statement: Residences aim to be a safe home and community, built on respect, sustainability, responsiveness, open communication, integrity, and honouring tradition.
74-university-residences-downtown-campus: Leases: August 20, 2026 to May 2, 2027 for first-years and exchange students; to June 30, 2027 for upper years and graduate students; Solin Hall, August 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
74-first-year-undergraduate-students: About 3,000 students, with 24-hour support, a Residence Council and wireless.
Traditional (meal plan, mostly single rooms with shared bathrooms): Gardner, McConnell, Molson, Douglas (quiet), Royal Victoria College (West Wing, women only), University Hall.
Hotel-style (meal plan, mostly doubles with en-suite): New Residence Hall, Carrefour Sherbrooke, La Citadelle. All You Care to Eat plan, plus oneCard Flex dollars.
Shared-facilities houses (quiet, singles, shared kitchens and laundry): 506/510/522 Pins Ave, 3653 and 3601 University.
Solin Hall (apartments with 2–4 bedrooms, no meal plan, oneCard dollars) is near Atwater Market and the Lachine Canal, four metro stops away.
75-upper-year-undergraduate-students: RVC Tower (meal plan) or Solin Hall. Also Greenbriar and Hutchison: studio and one-bedroom apartments, no meal plan, oneCard dollars.
75-graduate-students: Solin Hall; studios and one-bedrooms at Greenbriar, Hutchison, 3643 University and Rexford Hall; and shared-facilities houses with singles and shared kitchens. No mandatory meal plan, but oneCard dollars.
75-meal-plans: All You Care to Eat, with unlimited dine-in, is mandatory at Carrefour Sherbrooke, La Citadelle, Douglas, Gardner, Molson, McConnell, New Residence, Royal Victoria College and University Hall.
75-onecard: Linked to your ID for campus purchases, and due at the end of September. Flex dollars: $500 in meal plan residences, $600 in other downtown residences, $400 at Macdonald.
75-living-in-residences: Residence Life Facilitators, who are students, run activities to build community and support personal development.
75-contact-us: McGill Student Housing and Dining Service Centre, 3465 Durocher St. Requests go through the Service Desk portal.
75-student-government: Each hall elects a Residence Council at the start of the year to gather opinions, manage money, run activities and help set community standards. Everyone pays a $30 activity fee.
75-residence-fees: Options and prices are on the Student Housing site.
75-university-residences-macdonald-campu: Laird Hall and Eco Residence, for undergraduate, graduate and FMT students. Downtown students are welcome if there's room.
75-residence-options: Laird Hall: about 250 students, furnished rooms, shared kitchens and lounges.
Eco Residence: about 100, mainly upper-year and graduate students, furnished two- or six-bedroom split-level apartments.
Internet and laundry are included in both.
76-residence-occupancy-period: August 20, 2026 to May 2, 2027. Staying outside that needs approval and maybe a fee, in exceptional cases like extended sessions, Summer courses, campus jobs or travel constraints.
76-residence-fees: Billed separately but paid through your fee account. See the latest fee sheet.
76-food-services: No mandatory plan, but new students are charged $400 in oneCard dollars at the start of the lease. Eat at Twigs Café, between Macdonald-Stewart and Barton Library, or use the shared kitchens.
76-parking-macdonald-campus: Permits for students and staff only, from Laird Hall, Room 101, paid in person. You can send the form ahead by email.
76-macdonald-campus-residence-informatio: Residence Admissions Office: 21 111 Lakeshore, Room 107, Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, P.O. Box 188. Requests go through the Service Desk portal.
76-summer-accommodation: La Citadelle, 410 Sherbrooke W.: hotel-style, queen or two doubles, private bath, AC, Wi-Fi, 24-hour laundry and gym, shared kitchen (bring your own dishes).
Carrefour Sherbrooke, 475 Sherbrooke W.: hotel-style, one or two queens, private bath, AC, small fridge, daily housekeeping, gym, paid laundry.
Royal Victoria College, across from campus: private dorm rooms with twin bed, desk and small fridge, shared bath, kitchenettes and laundry.
77-reservations-for-summer-residences: Arriving before May 8 means at least a month's stay, paid in advance and non-refundable.
Cancel with the reservations office by noon ET on May 8 to avoid a one-night fee; telling another office doesn't count. Check availability before applying.
77-proper-use-of-computing-facilities: Follow the Policy on the Responsible Use of McGill IT Resources.
77-smoking-policy: Québec law bans smoking in public buildings, and on campus it's allowed only in outdoor designated areas. This includes e-cigarettes and similar devices.
77-policy-concerning-cannabis: Under the Policy Concerning Alcohol, Cannabis and Other Drugs, recreational cannabis is banned on all McGill property, including the Gault Nature Reserve and leased spaces. Medical use needs a valid certificate, under conditions.
77-incorporated-college: Royal Victoria College is a non-teaching, co-ed residential college.
77-affiliated-theological-colleges: Three colleges train for ministry and grant ordination certificates; they've handed degree-granting to McGill except for the M.Div. and honorary doctorates.
77-montreal-diocesan-theological-college: 3473 University St. Principal: Rev. Dr. Jesse Zink.
77-presbyterian-college-of-montreal: 3495 University St. Principal: Rev. Dr. Roland de Vries.
77-united-theological-college-of-montrea: 3475 University St. Principal: Rev. Maylanne Maybee.
77-libraries-and-historical-collections: Over 10 million print and electronic items across several locations, including the Visual Arts Collection. Bring your ID to borrow; e-resources work anywhere with your McGill login.
The site gives you thousands of databases, subject guides, digitized collections and eScholarship@McGill for theses and faculty work. Liaison librarians teach and answer questions.
Quiet and bookable group spaces, wireless, computers, printing and scanning, and longer hours at exams.
Course Readings Service links to readings in myCourses. Return books anywhere. Network and Interlibrary Loan are free for the McGill community.
78-workshops: Sessions and tours on using the library run through the year.
78-historical-collections: Listed on the Historical Collections page.
78-mcgill-writing-centre: McGill's central writing resource since 2010. Credit courses cover academic, creative, digital and business writing and communicating science, usable as electives or for language requirements in some degrees (some faculties need approval).
Also workshops, retreats and one-on-one consults.
78-mcgill-writing-centre-tutorial-servic: Help with writing and presentations at any stage, for all students.
78-mcgill-writing-centre-contact-informa: McLennan-Redpath Library, Main Floor, Room #02, 3459 McTavish St. Graphos has its own site and email.
78-service-point: Ground floor of the McLennan Library Building. Handles certified or translated diplomas, degree verification, admissions and Minerva help, insurance cards and exemptions, ID cards, transcript pick-up, replacement diplomas, exchanges, legal documents and fees.
Arts and Science students can also ask about registration and deferred or supplemental exams.
79-location: 3415 McTavish St., at Sherbrooke. Hours are on its site.
79-downtown-campus: Most services are in the Brown Student Services Building, Suite 4100, 3600 McTavish St.
79-campus-life-and-engagement-cl-e: Connects new and returning students to resources and opportunities. Suite 4100, Brown Building. First-years have their own email and getting-ready site.
79-career-planning-service-caps: Career education, events, advising, mentoring, workshops and the myFuture job board. Suite 2200, East Wing, and Centennial Centre, Room 124 at Macdonald; mention your campus when booking.
79-first-peoples-house: A community and voice for Indigenous students away from home, with academic, cultural and community support. Open to Métis, Inuit, First Nations (status and non-status), Maori and Aboriginal students, with no ID card needed. 3505 Peel St.
79-international-student-services-iss: Orientation, transition, immigration advice and health insurance guidance, plus tailored support for Mastercard Foundation Scholars.
Suite 4100 East Wing, Brown Building, and Centennial Centre, Room 124 at Macdonald. Write through the webform (immigration) or Insurance Portal ticket (insurance).
